summary: Steel tower built 1921 on Round Mountain near Marklesburg; register says moved in 1928 and renamed Rock Hill; no source read says where it stands now.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower was moved in 1928 and renamed Rock Hill. No source read says where it stands now or whether it still stands.

events.note: Steel tower built in 1921 in Huntingdon County, per the FFLOS register.
Mount Union Times item dated November 25, 1921 places the tower near Marklesburg and reports more than 100 students had recently climbed it.
Huntingdon Daily News item dated April 3, 1923 says Clyde Hecter and Chas. Ritenour would have charge of the fire tower on Round Knob for the next few months.
Register says the tower was moved in 1928 and renamed Rock Hill.

evidence.supports: built in 1921 as a steel tower, moved in 1928 and renamed Rock Hill

corrections.why: The register says the steel tower was moved in 1928 and renamed Rock Hill. It does not say the tower is no longer standing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the record Round Mountain Tower Site; the history page calls it Round Mountain (Knob); the 1923 item says Round Knob. The story uses Round Mountain.

notes_for_editor: Rock Hill destination is unresolved. The Huntingdon Daily News column on the retired Rockhill fire tower near Wood (Fulton County, Broad Top Mountain) could identify it, but fetch_text and WebFetch both returned HTTP 429 for that URL, so it was not read; retry before publishing. Do not confuse with the 1920 wooden Rockhill tower near Robertsdale, which is a different structure on the Rockhill history page. The 1923 item's wording about farms is unclear, so the story quotes it only for the fire tower charge. Brief status gone is proposed as relocated.
